steps: Tables arrange data in rows and columns, making it easy to organise and compare values.
Charts present data visually, helping us notice patterns, differences, and trends quickly.
For example, students’ marks in different subjects can be entered in a table, with students as rows and subjects as columns.
A bar chart of the same marks can show how each student performed in each subject.
To draw the bar chart, label the horizontal axis with the subjects and the vertical axis with marks; draw a separate bar for each student in every subject and include a key.
items.finalAnswer: Tables organise data for comparison, while charts show patterns and differences visually; students’ subject grades can be presented in a table or bar chart.

steps: Non-numeric data is essential when studying information that consists of qualities, descriptions, opinions, or categories rather than numbers.
For example, a school may want to understand students’ opinions about the library facilities.
Collect the data by asking clear questions in a survey or interview and recording students’ responses accurately.
Store the responses in a spreadsheet or database, using one record for each response and a field for each question.
Check the responses for missing, duplicate, or unclear entries, while protecting students’ privacy.
Analyse the data by grouping similar responses into categories and counting or comparing the responses in each category.
Use tables, bar charts, or word summaries to present the findings; review the original responses to ensure that the categories and conclusions represent what students said.
items.finalAnswer: Collect responses through surveys or interviews, store them systematically, and analyse them by categorising and comparing the responses.

steps: Data visualization is the presentation of data in a graphical or visual form, such as charts, graphs, maps, or dashboards.
It helps people understand complex data by showing patterns, comparisons, relationships, and trends clearly.
A bar chart can compare the sales of different products in a shop.
A line graph can show how temperature changes over time or how a company’s sales change from month to month.
A pie chart can show how a household budget is divided among expenses.
A map can show differences in population or rainfall across regions.
A dashboard can bring together several charts and key figures to help managers monitor business performance.
items.finalAnswer: Data visualization presents data visually so patterns, comparisons, and trends are easier to understand; examples include bar charts, line graphs, pie charts, maps, and dashboards.

steps: Data visualization presents data in a form that is easier to understand than a large collection of raw values.
Charts and graphs help people identify patterns, trends, comparisons, and unusual results quickly.
Visual presentations make complex information clearer and help communicate findings to others.
Businesses use dashboards to bring important information, such as sales and expenses, together in one place.
Decision-makers use charts, graphs, and dashboards to compare results, monitor performance, and make informed decisions.
items.finalAnswer: Data visualization makes information clear and helps businesses and decision-makers identify trends, compare results, monitor performance, and make informed decisions.

steps: Nominal data consists of named categories with no natural order, such as types of transport. A bar chart can compare the number of students using each type of transport.

Ordinal data consists of categories that have a meaningful order, such as satisfaction ratings of poor, fair, good, and excellent. An ordered bar chart can display the number of responses in each rating category.
Discrete data consists of countable values, usually whole numbers, such as the number of books borrowed by each student. A bar chart can show the number of students for each number of books borrowed.
Continuous data can take any value within a range, such as students’ heights. A histogram can group heights into intervals and show the frequency in each interval.
items.finalAnswer: Nominal data has unordered categories, ordinal data has ordered categories, discrete data is countable, and continuous data can take any value within a range; bar charts, ordered bar charts, bar charts, and histograms respectively can display them.
